content.text: The profile shows one failing rule: `plan_code` has 8 rows with `GOLD`, which the contract's `allowed` list doesn't include. Everything else passes. I'll validate a candidate that adds `GOLD` to `plan_code`'s allowed values and bumps the version.

input.contract_yaml:
# Member eligibility from a (synthetic) payer: one row per member, one file per day.
# Generated from the Synthea patients by packs/healthcare/generators/eligibility.py.
feed: healthcare.eligibility
version: 2
owner: vendor-ops@example.com
description: >
  Daily full eligibility file: every enrolled member with their plan and coverage dates.
  All data is synthetic.
classification: restricted
source:
  channels: [minio, sftp, api]
  filename_pattern: "elig_*.csv"
  # The business date in the name (elig_YYYYMMDD.csv). It must be a real date, not after
  # the day the file was received, and at most 7 days before it; otherwise the file is
  # quarantined (FILE.NAME_DATE). A name with no digits takes the date it was received.
  filename_date:
    regex: "^elig_([0-9]+)"
    format: "%Y%m%d"
    max_days_before_received: 7
    max_days_after_received: 0
format: { type: csv, delimiter: ",", encoding: utf-8, header: true }
expected_arrival: { cron: "0 6 * * *", grace: 2h }
on_row_violation: quarantine_row
max_bad_row_ratio: 0.05          # above this, the whole file is rejected
min_rows: 1
columns:
  - { name: member_id, type: string, required: true, unique: true, pattern: "^M[0-9]{9}$" }
  - { name: first_name, type: string, required: true, phi: true }
  - { name: last_name, type: string, required: true, phi: true }
  - { name: dob, type: date, required: true, min: "1900-01-01", max: today, phi: true }
  - { name: sex, type: string, required: true, allowed: [F, M, U] }
  - { name: plan_code, type: string, required: true, allowed: [HMO, PPO, EPO, HDHP, GOLD] }
  - { name: coverage_start, type: date, required: true, min: "1990-01-01" }
  - { name: coverage_end, type: date, description: "Empty while coverage is open" }
  - name: patient_ref
    type: string
    description: The payer's link to the clinical record (here the Synthea patient id)
    phi: true

input.rationale: Drift in elig_20261021.csv (job 1): the file has the same 9 columns in the same order as the contract, with no missing or unexpected columns. The only failing rule is plan_code: 8 of 24 rows carry GOLD, which is not in the allowed list [HMO, PPO, EPO, HDHP]. GOLD is a clean, consistent plan tier name in every GOLD row, not junk or malformed text, and the other columns show no change, so I read it as a deliberate new plan tier. Without a change the 8 rows would be quarantined (33%, above the 5% max_bad_row_ratio), so the whole file would be rejected. Change: plan_code allowed adds GOLD; version 1 -> 2. Loosening: plan_code.allowed gains GOLD. This is the only loosening, and it is needed for the vendor's new value. Nothing else is changed. Dry run: 24 accepted, 0 rejected, file not rejected. Reviewer note: the profile labels member_id phi: true, but the contract has no phi flag on it. I left it unchanged because the drift rules keep existing columns as they are; it may need a separate review.

content.text:
The vendor added a new plan tier: 8 of 24 rows carry `GOLD` in `plan_code`, which the contract didn't allow. Nothing else changed; the columns and their order match. I treated `GOLD` as a deliberate change, since it's a clean, consistent value and not junk. Without a change, those 8 rows would have been quarantined (33%, above the 5% limit), so the whole file would have been rejected.

The candidate adds `GOLD` to `plan_code`'s allowed values and bumps the version to 2. That is the only loosening. The dry run accepted 24 rows and rejected 0. I submitted it for review (candidate `e4d8a99990deee94`).

I also flagged that the profile labels `member_id` as PHI, but the contract doesn't mark it. I left it unchanged, since drift edits keep existing columns' rules, and a reviewer should decide whether it needs a `phi` flag.
